entries.title: Respirology Acronyms

testable_competencies.reference_use: Expand common respiratory abbreviations when encountered in clinical material.

entries.zero_question_reason: Acronym expansion is reference support, not an independent clinical question target.

entries.title: Basic Respiratory Anatomy

testable_competencies.anatomic_localization: Use basic airway, alveolar, pleural, and thoracic anatomy to localize common respiratory problems.

entries.zero_question_reason: Foundational anatomy should be assessed only inside clinical questions, not as standalone recall.

entries.title: Differential Diagnosis of Common Respiratory Presentations

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The unit directly operationalizes the Dyspnea objective's requirement to identify life-threatening causes, distinguish pulmonary/cardiac/other causes, investigate, and initiate management.
The source's presentation-based differential directly supports the Cough objective's acute/subacute/chronic discrimination and serious-cause assessment.
The chest-pain differential directly supports exclusion of life-threatening pulmonary and cardiovascular causes.
Hemoptysis differential and urgency assessment directly match the objective's stabilization-versus-investigation decision.

testable_competencies.triage: Recognize unstable or life-threatening respiratory presentations and prioritize immediate assessment.
testable_competencies.differential: Construct a focused differential for dyspnea, cough, chest pain, and hemoptysis using acuity and key clinical features.
testable_competencies.initial_workup: Choose initial investigations that distinguish common pulmonary, cardiac, and other causes.

entries.title: Basic Pulmonary Function Test Interpretation

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The Cough objective explicitly includes pulmonary function testing among critical investigations, while this unit teaches the interpretation component rather than the full cough presentation.
Basic PFT interpretation supports chronic dyspnea evaluation, though the Dyspnea objective names other initial investigations more explicitly.

testable_competencies.pattern_interpretation: Distinguish obstructive, restrictive, mixed, and diffusion abnormalities on basic pulmonary function data.
testable_competencies.clinical_integration: Relate a basic PFT pattern to the presenting respiratory syndrome and decide when further testing or referral is needed.

do_not_test: Rare flow-volume-loop variants without generalist decision value

entries.title: Basic Chest Radiograph Patterns

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The Dyspnea objective explicitly requires chest-radiograph interpretation; this unit supplies that investigation component.
The Cough objective explicitly includes appropriate imaging, supported here by basic CXR pattern recognition.

testable_competencies.pattern_recognition: Recognize basic consolidation, interstitial, nodular, pleural, hyperinflation, and collapse patterns on a chest radiograph.
testable_competencies.next_step: Use the radiographic pattern with clinical context to select appropriate further assessment or referral.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Shared with Medical Imaging; R retains the generalist ability to recognize basic patterns and act on urgent findings, without assigning global ownership.

entries.title: Arterial Blood Gases, Acid-Base Status, and Hypoxemia

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective explicitly requires evaluation of hypoxemia/hypoxia, interpretation of the A-a gradient, resuscitation, treatment of cause, and referral.
The Dyspnea objective explicitly lists ABGs among critical investigations; acid-base interpretation is a component of that broader presentation.

testable_competencies.abg_interpretation: Interpret pH, PaCO2, bicarbonate, compensation, and oxygenation in common respiratory presentations.
testable_competencies.hypoxemia_mechanism: Use the A-a gradient and response to oxygen conceptually to distinguish hypoventilation, V/Q mismatch, diffusion impairment, and shunt.
testable_competencies.urgent_action: Recognize severe hypoxemia or ventilatory failure and initiate stabilization and escalation.

do_not_test: Isolated compensation-formula recall without a clinical decision

entries.title: Pneumonia (Respiratory Cross-Reference)

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pneumonia is explicitly named as a pulmonary parenchymal cause in the Dyspnea objective.
Acute infectious cough is explicitly within the Cough objective, though pneumonia is not named there.
The Fever objective covers infectious presentations, chest radiography, antimicrobial treatment, and escalation, but is broader than pneumonia.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize pneumonia as a cause of cough, fever, dyspnea, hypoxemia, and parapneumonic complications.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Assess severity, choose initial investigations, begin appropriate initial management, and identify need for admission or referral.

clinical_source_organizations: Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada
entries.cross_discipline_note: The R source is cross-reference-only to Pediatrics; adult/community infection scope overlaps ID, ER, Pediatrics, and FM and is not globally assigned here.
entries.zero_question_reason: The R source contains no substantive pneumonia teaching; coverage should come from the linked disease-owning chapter(s), not be duplicated from this cross-reference.

entries.title: Asthma

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Asthma is explicitly named in the Dyspnea objective's airway causes and the objective requires urgent and chronic management.
Cough-variant asthma is explicitly named in the Cough objective, which also requires PFTs, medication, counselling, and referral decisions.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize asthma and confirm variable airflow limitation using appropriate objective testing.
testable_competencies.control_and_risk: Assess symptom control, exacerbation risk, triggers, adherence, and inhaler technique.
testable_competencies.acute_management: Recognize and initially stabilize an acute severe exacerbation, including escalation when response is inadequate.
testable_competencies.longitudinal_management: Develop an individualized controller and prevention plan with follow-up.

do_not_test: Exact inhaler sequencing or doses without current Canadian guideline verification

entries.title: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: COPD is explicitly named as an airway cause of dyspnea, with the objective covering acute stabilization, chronic management, prevention, and complications.
Chronic pulmonary cough and PFT assessment are within the Cough objective; COPD is a common instantiation but not named verbatim.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize COPD, confirm persistent airflow obstruction, and assess symptoms and exacerbation risk.
testable_competencies.exacerbation: Identify and initially manage an acute COPD exacerbation, including respiratory-failure risk and escalation.
testable_competencies.longitudinal_management: Plan smoking cessation, vaccination, inhaled therapy, rehabilitation, oxygen assessment, and follow-up at a generalist level.

clinical_source_organizations: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease
do_not_test: Exact inhaler sequencing, oxygen targets, or home-NIV protocols without current Canadian verification

entries.title: Bronchiectasis

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Bronchiectasis is explicitly named as an inflammatory airway cause of hemoptysis, including urgent assessment and specialist-referral decisions.
The chronic pulmonary cough framework supports bronchiectasis evaluation but does not name the condition.
Dyspnea assessment and investigation provide a broader presentation anchor for symptomatic bronchiectasis.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize bronchiectasis from chronic productive cough, recurrent infection, hemoptysis, and characteristic imaging.
testable_competencies.initial_management: Obtain appropriate cultures and imaging, begin airway-clearance and infection management, and identify complications requiring specialist care.

do_not_test: Specialist eradication regimens or long-term antibiotic schedules without current guidance

entries.title: Cystic Fibrosis

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cystic fibrosis is explicitly named as a V/Q-mismatch cause of central cyanosis or hypoxemia.
Chronic pulmonary dyspnea evaluation supports recognition of advanced CF lung disease but does not name CF.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize cystic fibrosis from recurrent respiratory infection, malabsorption, and characteristic diagnostic testing.
testable_competencies.complications: Identify pulmonary and multisystem complications that require specialist multidisciplinary care.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Shared with Pediatrics and Clinical Pharmacology; R preserves recognition of pulmonary manifestations and complications without final ownership assignment.

entries.title: General Approach to Interstitial Lung Disease

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Parenchymal/interstitial disease and pneumonitis are explicitly named dyspnea causes; the objective includes exposure history, imaging, ABGs, referral, and chronic planning.
Diffusion impairment from restrictive lung disease is explicitly named as a mechanism of hypoxemia, with A-a gradient interpretation and escalation.
Chronic pulmonary cough and work-related exposure are within the Cough objective, supporting part of this unit.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize an interstitial/restrictive presentation from progressive exertional dyspnea, dry cough, examination, imaging, and PFT findings.
testable_competencies.etiologic_assessment: Elicit connective-tissue, occupational, environmental, medication, and treatment exposures and select initial investigations.
testable_competencies.referral: Identify progressive hypoxemia or uncertain ILD requiring specialist assessment.

do_not_test: Rare ILD taxonomy or obscure histopathology

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: IPF is an interstitial cause of chronic dyspnea fitting the objective's explicit parenchymal/interstitial category, but it is not named specifically.
IPF produces diffusion-limited hypoxemia within the objective's explicit restrictive-lung-disease category, but the disease is not named.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a typical IPF presentation and usual interstitial pneumonia pattern at a generalist level.
testable_competencies.next_step: Exclude common alternative exposures or systemic causes, assess oxygenation, and refer for specialist confirmation and management.

entries.title: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pneumonitis and occupational/environmental exposure history are explicit in the Dyspnea objective, but hypersensitivity pneumonitis is not named.
The Work-related health objective directly requires exposure history, PFT/imaging assessment, work modification, treatment, and referral for occupational illness.

testable_competencies.exposure_link: Recognize temporal links between inhaled occupational or hobby antigen exposure and respiratory symptoms.
testable_competencies.initial_assessment: Select basic imaging and pulmonary testing, remove exposure, and refer when disease is severe, progressive, or diagnostically uncertain.

clinical_source_organizations: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Sarcoidosis is a parenchymal/interstitial cause of dyspnea within the objective's explicit category, but it is not named specifically.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize common pulmonary and extrapulmonary sarcoidosis patterns and important mimics.
testable_competencies.initial_workup: Choose appropriate initial imaging and laboratory assessment and identify organ involvement requiring urgent referral.

entries.title: Pneumoconioses and Occupational Fibrotic Lung Disease

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective explicitly names asbestos and requires workplace attribution, imaging/PFTs, work advice, compensation, reporting, and referral.
Occupational exposure history and chronic dyspnea assessment are explicit, while individual pneumoconioses are not named.
Work-related exposure is explicitly part of chronic cough assessment and counselling.

testable_competencies.exposure_history: Take a specific occupational and environmental exposure history for asbestos, silica, coal, and related hazards.
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize common radiographic and clinical patterns and major complications, including malignancy and infection risk.
testable_competencies.management: Remove or reduce exposure, initiate appropriate surveillance/referral, and address work and prevention implications.

clinical_source_organizations: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety
entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps Public Health/occupational medicine and Thoracic Surgery/oncology; chapter-level classification does not settle global ownership.

entries.title: Drug- and Treatment-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Drug-related pneumonitis is encompassed by the objective's explicit pneumonitis/interstitial dyspnea category, though specific agents are not listed.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize medication or radiation exposure as a potential cause of new interstitial respiratory symptoms and imaging abnormalities.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Review culprit exposure, assess severity and oxygenation, stop or withhold a suspected agent when safe, and seek specialist input.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pulmonary hypertension commonly presents through dyspnea and requires the objective's cardiopulmonary differentiation and referral, but it is not named in that objective.
Pulmonary hypertension is explicitly named as an obstructive cause of shock, supporting recognition of decompensation but not the entire chronic disease unit.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize pulmonary hypertension from progressive dyspnea, exertional syncope, right-heart findings, and suggestive tests.
testable_competencies.initial_workup: Assess common cardiac, pulmonary, thromboembolic, systemic, and medication causes and arrange confirmatory specialist evaluation.
testable_competencies.urgency: Recognize decompensated right-heart failure or high-risk symptoms requiring urgent referral.

entries.title: Pulmonary Embolism

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pulmonary embolism is explicitly named as a pulmonary vascular cause of dyspnea and the objective requires urgent assessment and management.
Pulmonary embolism/infarction is explicitly named under chest pain, including urgent therapy and referral.
Pulmonary embolism with infarction is explicitly named as a hemoptysis cause.
Pulmonary embolus is explicitly named as an obstructive cause of shock requiring timely cause-specific management.
The localized edema objective explicitly prioritizes proximal DVT, the common source condition in PE evaluation.

testable_competencies.risk_assessment: Estimate pretest probability using history, examination, and validated decision tools in appropriate patients.
testable_competencies.diagnosis: Select and interpret D-dimer and imaging based on pretest probability and contraindications.
testable_competencies.initial_management: Begin timely anticoagulation when appropriate, recognize hemodynamic instability, stabilize, and escalate for reperfusion or specialist care.
testable_competencies.disposition: Risk-stratify confirmed PE and identify patients requiring admission versus potential outpatient care.

do_not_test: Exact anticoagulant doses or treatment duration without current Canadian verification

entries.title: Pulmonary Vasculitis and Alveolar Hemorrhage

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Vasculitis is explicitly named as an inflammatory/immune cause of hemoptysis, including stabilization, systemic testing, and referral.
Pulmonary parenchymal disease causing dyspnea provides a broader presentation anchor for vasculitic lung involvement.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize pulmonary-renal, upper-airway, eosinophilic, or diffuse-alveolar-hemorrhage patterns suggesting systemic vasculitis or anti-GBM disease.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Assess airway and oxygenation, obtain targeted urinalysis/renal function/serology/imaging, and arrange urgent specialty care for organ-threatening disease.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantial overlap with Rheumatology and Nephrology; R retains pulmonary recognition, stabilization, and referral scope without final ownership assignment.

entries.title: Pulmonary Edema (Cardiology Cross-Reference)

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Acute pulmonary edema fits life-threatening cardiopulmonary dyspnea assessment, though the objective does not name pulmonary edema verbatim.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize pulmonary edema as an urgent cause of dyspnea and hypoxemia and distinguish likely cardiogenic from noncardiogenic context.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Stabilize oxygenation and ventilation, identify the precipitating cause, and escalate appropriately.

entries.cross_discipline_note: The R source explicitly defers to Cardiology; R preserves respiratory recognition and stabilization only.
entries.zero_question_reason: The source is a pure Cardiology cross-reference, so independent R question coverage would duplicate the owning chapter.

entries.title: Mediastinal Masses (Thoracic Surgery Cross-Reference)

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The unit directly matches the Mediastinal mass objective's compartment-based differential, severity assessment, investigation, and management plan.

testable_competencies.recognition: Use mediastinal compartment and clinical features to frame a differential and identify compressive or malignant warning signs.
testable_competencies.next_step: Select initial imaging and refer for definitive evaluation when a mediastinal mass is suspected.

entries.cross_discipline_note: The R node defers to General and Thoracic Surgery; R retains recognition and initial investigation only.
entries.zero_question_reason: The source is primarily a Thoracic Surgery cross-reference; coverage should be coordinated with that chapter.

entries.title: Mediastinitis

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The Chest pain objective includes pulmonary or mediastinal causes and urgent exclusion of serious disease, but does not name mediastinitis.
Fever from serious infection, targeted imaging, antimicrobial treatment, and specialized care support the infectious presentation component.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize acute mediastinitis after esophageal/tracheal perforation, infection spread, or thoracic procedures.
testable_competencies.urgent_action: Initiate stabilization, broad initial investigation and antimicrobial care, and urgent surgical consultation.

clinical_source_organizations: Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada
do_not_test: Exact empiric antibiotic regimen without current verification

entries.title: Pleural Effusion, Parapneumonic Effusion, and Empyema

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit directly matches the Pleural effusion objective, which explicitly includes parapneumonic effusion and empyema, fluid analysis, underlying-cause treatment, drainage, and thoracic referral.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize pleural effusion clinically and radiographically and distinguish likely transudative from exudative causes.
testable_competencies.fluid_interpretation: Interpret basic pleural fluid results to identify infection, malignancy, and other important causes.
testable_competencies.management: Treat the underlying cause and identify indications for drainage, admission, or thoracic consultation.

clinical_source_organizations: Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada
do_not_test: Exact pleural-fluid thresholds without current source verification

entries.title: Atelectasis (Thoracic Surgery Cross-Reference)

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Atelectasis is explicitly named as a pulmonary parenchymal cause of dyspnea.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize atelectasis as a cause of dyspnea, hypoxemia, and characteristic volume-loss imaging findings.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Identify the likely mechanism and address reversible causes while escalating if respiratory compromise is present.

entries.cross_discipline_note: The source defers to General and Thoracic Surgery; R retains recognition and initial respiratory management.
entries.zero_question_reason: The R source is cross-reference-only and does not support independent detailed coverage.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pneumothorax is explicitly named as a pleural cause of dyspnea, including life-threatening presentations.
Pneumothorax is explicitly named as a chest-pain cause requiring urgent therapy.
Tension pneumothorax is explicitly named as an obstructive cause of shock.
The Chest injuries objective explicitly names tension pneumothorax and requires resuscitation before deferred investigations.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize spontaneous or traumatic pneumothorax and the clinical diagnosis of tension pneumothorax.
testable_competencies.stabilization: Provide immediate stabilization for tension physiology without delaying for imaging and arrange definitive pleural management.
testable_competencies.investigation: Use appropriate imaging for stable suspected pneumothorax and recognize complications.

entries.title: Asbestos-Related Pleural Disease and Mesothelioma

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The Pleural effusion objective explicitly names mesothelioma and occupational/environmental exposure assessment.
The Work-related health objective explicitly names asbestos and requires exposure attribution, investigation, work advice, and referral.
Asbestos exposure is explicitly a hemoptysis risk factor and bronchogenic malignancy is an explicit serious cause.

testable_competencies.exposure_history: Elicit asbestos exposure and latency and recognize benign pleural disease versus features concerning for mesothelioma.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Arrange appropriate imaging, pleural assessment, exposure counselling, and specialist referral.

clinical_source_organizations: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety
entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps occupational medicine, oncology, and Thoracic Surgery; R retains pulmonary/pleural recognition and referral without assigning global ownership.

entries.title: Hypoxemic and Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective directly covers hypoxemia/hypoxia mechanisms, critical illness resuscitation, treatment of cause, and specialized referral; hypoventilation is explicitly named.
The unit directly supports the Dyspnea objective's ABC assessment, ABG interpretation, emergent management, and escalation for life-threatening respiratory illness.

testable_competencies.recognition: Distinguish hypoxemic from hypercapnic respiratory failure using clinical findings and ABGs and identify acute-on-chronic physiology.
testable_competencies.stabilization: Support airway, oxygenation, and ventilation while treating reversible causes and escalating to noninvasive or invasive support when needed.
testable_competencies.monitoring: Recognize deterioration and complications requiring critical-care referral.

do_not_test: Exact ventilator settings or specialist protocols
Fixed oxygen targets without current guideline verification

entries.title: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: ARDS is explicitly named as an intrapulmonary shunt cause of central cyanosis/hypoxemia requiring resuscitation and treatment.
ARDS is explicitly named as a pulmonary parenchymal cause of dyspnea requiring urgent management.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize ARDS from acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, bilateral opacities, and a noncardiogenic context.
testable_competencies.initial_management: Treat the precipitating cause, initiate lung-protective supportive care principles, and involve critical care early.
testable_competencies.complications: Recognize refractory hypoxemia and ventilation-related complications.

do_not_test: Specialist ventilation settings, paralysis, proning, or ECMO protocols
Exact diagnostic thresholds without current verification

entries.title: Lung Cancer (Thoracic Surgery Cross-Reference)

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Bronchogenic carcinoma is explicitly named as a hemoptysis cause; smoking and asbestos exposure, chest imaging, CT, stabilization, and specialist referral are also explicit.
Pulmonary/mediastinal malignancy is explicitly a chest-pain cause, but that objective covers only one presentation slice of lung cancer.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize symptoms, signs, imaging abnormalities, and exposure risks concerning for lung cancer.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Arrange appropriate initial imaging and urgent referral while addressing smoking and occupational risk.

clinical_source_organizations: Canadian Task Force on Preventive Health Care
do_not_test: Screening schedules without current Canadian verification
entries.cross_discipline_note: The source explicitly defers to General and Thoracic Surgery; R retains recognition, initial investigation, and referral.
entries.zero_question_reason: The R node is a pure cross-reference; independent detailed oncology coverage would duplicate the linked chapter.

entries.title: Solitary Pulmonary Nodule (Imaging and Surgery Cross-Reference)

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The Hemoptysis objective supports CT evaluation for serious underlying bronchogenic malignancy, but it does not address an incidental solitary pulmonary nodule or its follow-up algorithm.

testable_competencies.risk_assessment: Recognize patient and imaging factors that make a pulmonary nodule more concerning for malignancy.
testable_competencies.next_step: Arrange comparison imaging and appropriate imaging/specialist follow-up using a current validated pathway.

do_not_test: Exact size thresholds or surveillance intervals without current Canadian verification
entries.cross_discipline_note: The R source is cross-reference-only to Medical Imaging and Thoracic Surgery; no global owner is selected here.
entries.zero_question_reason: The source contains no independent nodule algorithm; detailed question coverage belongs with the linked imaging/surgical material.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hypoventilation is explicitly named as a normal-A-a-gradient cause of hypoxemia, with resuscitation, cause treatment, and referral.
Sleep-disordered breathing is explicitly within the Sleep-wake disorders objective, including specialized testing, management, and safety.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize sleep-related hypoventilation due to obesity, medications, neuromuscular, chest-wall, neurologic, or severe lung disease.
testable_competencies.assessment: Assess daytime hypercapnia, oxygenation, medication contributors, and need for formal sleep or respiratory testing.
testable_competencies.management: Treat reversible causes and refer for ventilatory support assessment when indicated.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Sleep-disordered breathing is explicitly within the objective, including history, polysomnography, management counselling, and daytime-somnolence safety screening.

testable_competencies.recognition: Identify obstructive versus central sleep-apnea risk factors and clinical consequences.
testable_competencies.diagnosis: Choose appropriate sleep testing and interpret a basic diagnostic result at a generalist level.
testable_competencies.management: Counsel on safety and modifiable risks, initiate appropriate first-line planning, and refer when needed.

entries.title: Intensive Care Unit Basics

testable_competencies.escalation_context: Recognize when hemodynamic, respiratory, or cardiac instability requires intensive monitoring and specialist support.

entries.zero_question_reason: ICU organization and monitoring context should be embedded in acute-care questions rather than tested independently.

entries.title: Critical Care Lines and Catheters

testable_competencies.device_awareness: Recognize the broad purpose and major complications of arterial, central venous, and pulmonary artery catheters.

entries.zero_question_reason: Detailed critical-care vascular access and hemodynamic monitoring are specialist procedural content.

entries.title: Recognition of Multisystem Organ Failure

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize common clinical and laboratory signals of respiratory, cardiac, renal, hepatic, and coagulation failure in a critically ill patient.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps Cardiology, Nephrology, Gastroenterology, Hematology, ER, and critical care; no global ownership is assigned.
entries.zero_question_reason: The table is cross-system context; definitive organ-specific competencies are mapped in their respective chapters.

entries.title: Shock: Recognition and Initial Stabilization

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The unit directly matches the Shock objective's cause/severity assessment, urgency recognition, critical investigations, perfusion restoration, and cause-specific treatment.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize compensated and uncompensated shock and distinguish hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive, and obstructive patterns.
testable_competencies.initial_management: Restore perfusion while rapidly identifying and treating the underlying cause and reassessing response.

do_not_test: Fixed fluid or vasopressor protocols without current verification
entries.cross_discipline_note: Strong overlap with ER, Cardiology, and critical care; chapter-level DIRECT classification does not settle global ownership.

entries.title: Sepsis and Septic Shock

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Sepsis is explicitly named as a distributive cause in the Shock objective, which requires timely perfusion restoration and treatment of the underlying cause.
The Fever objective covers life-threatening infection, targeted cultures/imaging, antimicrobials, and specialized care, but not the full sepsis syndrome.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize suspected infection with organ dysfunction and identify septic shock.
testable_competencies.initial_management: Obtain appropriate cultures without harmful delay, start timely empiric therapy, restore perfusion, and pursue source control and critical-care escalation.
testable_competencies.reassessment: Monitor response and revise therapy as diagnostic information becomes available.

clinical_source_organizations: Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada
do_not_test: Exact antimicrobial regimens, fluid volumes, MAP targets, or vasopressor sequences without current verification
entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps ER and Infectious Diseases; R retains acute respiratory/critical-care recognition and initial action without global ownership assignment.

entries.title: Common Respiratory and ICU Medications

testable_competencies.safe_reference_use: Use a current authoritative source to verify indications, contraindications, interactions, adverse effects, and dosing before prescribing respiratory or ICU medications.

entries.zero_question_reason: The source is a volatile medication reference table; exact details must be researched source-first during question generation.

entries.title: Landmark Respirology Trials

testable_competencies.evidence_context: Recognize that major respiratory recommendations arise from evolving evidence and verify current guidance rather than memorizing historical trial minutiae.

do_not_test: Trial acronyms, sample sizes, effect estimates, or publication-year recall
entries.zero_question_reason: Historical trial summaries are reference material and not independent generalist clinical competencies.
